candidate_answer: The dashed projection shortcuts in residual networks (a) enable gradients to bypass intermediate layers directly, preventing vanishing gradients. In contrast, inception-like networks (b) lack such shortcuts, forcing gradients to propagate through all layers, which constrains flow and increases vanishing gradient risk.
reference: Deep residual networks have skip connections that allow the gradient to flow directly from one layer to another, while networks built by stacking inception-like blocks do not.
